# Transfer and retention

Use a new domain to test the same concept. These tasks supplement the existing 72 exercises; they do not replace stage gates. Attempt without your Signal Desk solution, then use the criteria. No model is required unless your chosen evidence claim depends on one.

## Stage 1 · A meeting action-list assistant

Given “Mara will investigate the slow build; no deadline agreed,” design a bounded task contract and a three-responsibility diagram. The tool can save a local list but cannot assign work or send messages. Include one missing fact and one verification step.

**Pass criteria:** Preserve investigation versus completion; Do not invent a deadline or communication authority; Make information flows and done conditions observable.

**Recall target:** Confusing generated suggestions with completed actions.

**Delayed variation:** change one decisive fact, predict the changed outcome before checking notes, and explain why the original reasoning needs to change.

## Stage 2 · A sourced research note

Sources: R1 says a museum was closed Monday for maintenance; R2 says its normal schedule is Tuesday–Sunday; R3 is a two-year-old blog claiming daily opening. Prepare a packet answering whether it is open next Monday. Retain dates, authority, and uncertainty; state the next evidence needed.

**Pass criteria:** Distinguish usual schedule, one-off closure, and stale blog; Avoid an unsupported future-hours promise; Preserve provenance in the compressed packet.

**Recall target:** Treating freshness or one source mention as sufficient support.

**Delayed variation:** change one decisive fact, predict the changed outcome before checking notes, and explain why the original reasoning needs to change.

## Stage 3 · A library recommendation tool

Specify lookup_book and save_reading_list for a local catalog. Include absent record, invalid identifier, and repeated save. Draft a skill activation boundary with one positive and one negative request. Do not implement checkout.

**Pass criteria:** Define exact input/output and effect contracts; Separate discovery from authority; Demonstrate or mechanically trace rejection before effect.

**Recall target:** Equating capability discovery or skill text with execution permission.

**Delayed variation:** change one decisive fact, predict the changed outcome before checking notes, and explain why the original reasoning needs to change.

## Stage 4 · Review a QA change

A proposed patch changes quantity validation from quantity > 0 to quantity >= 0. Write a behavior brief, two tests that distinguish versions, and a review note. State which requirement you must clarify before calling this a fix.

**Pass criteria:** Clarify whether zero is valid instead of guessing; Use behavioral boundary tests; Tie review conclusion to requirement and executed or manual evidence.

**Recall target:** Calling any changed behavior a verified improvement.

**Delayed variation:** change one decisive fact, predict the changed outcome before checking notes, and explain why the original reasoning needs to change.

## Stage 5 · A document extraction checkpoint

A local extractor saved page 3 then lost its response. Design an operation record and restart sequence for pages 1–4. Include a replay with changed input, a step limit, and incomplete output status.

**Pass criteria:** Separate effect from acknowledgement; Detect changed input and avoid duplicate accepted effects; Preserve partial work and truthful stop status.

**Recall target:** Assuming a timeout means no effect occurred.

**Delayed variation:** change one decisive fact, predict the changed outcome before checking notes, and explain why the original reasoning needs to change.

## Stage 6 · Grade a research summary

Create six short claims against two sources: two supported, two unsupported, and two disputed. Freeze labels before comparing two grading approaches. Report disagreements and define a severe-failure gate.

**Pass criteria:** Separate exact source existence from semantic support; Keep disputed cases explicit; Report denominators and contamination limits.

**Recall target:** Mistaking fluent answers or aggregate scores for reliable evaluation.

**Delayed variation:** change one decisive fact, predict the changed outcome before checking notes, and explain why the original reasoning needs to change.

## Stage 7 · Two reviewers of an invoice extraction

Assign an arithmetic checker and a source-completeness checker separate inputs and directories. Deliver one stale result and one duplicate result. Compare the integrated artifact with one reviewer on the same pages.

**Pass criteria:** Record complete input versions and integration ownership; Reject stale/duplicate effects; Include parent effort and correlated error risk.

**Recall target:** Treating multiple agreeing workers as independent verification.

**Delayed variation:** change one decisive fact, predict the changed outcome before checking notes, and explain why the original reasoning needs to change.

## Stage 8 · Release a local research notebook

Prepare a release for a sourced-note generator using synthetic documents. Simulate a source-version update while one note is pending. Rehearse rollback and produce a dossier another person can inspect.

**Pass criteria:** Approval or release record identifies the exact artifact/source versions; Pending work survives rollback; Recovery and limits are supported by reproducible or clearly manual evidence.

**Recall target:** Calling a demonstration production ready without an operating boundary.

**Delayed variation:** change one decisive fact, predict the changed outcome before checking notes, and explain why the original reasoning needs to change.

## Build a mistake-driven recall queue

After feedback, choose one misconception, write a new-case question that would expose it, and save the original attempt. Use the portal recall queue or the [offline recall template](../../templates/recall-queue.md). Record the next review date, help used, result, and one next action.

Begin with a revisit in your next available session. After independent success, choose a longer interval; after a hint or repeated error, shorten the interval and simplify the prompt. Increasing intervals are a practical starting approach, not a universal timing law. Observe your actual recall and adjust.

Before answering, predict your confidence. Afterwards, record what changed your mind. A card can leave the active queue when you solve a new case after a delay and explain the earlier error; keep its history. No automated schedule substitutes for an actual recall attempt.
